schema.text: Adults with newly diagnosed breast, colorectal, melanoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or NSCLC planning systemic chemotherapy (including targeted therapy) and/or PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4 checkpoint inhibitors. Enrollment allowed up to the start of cycle 2.

schema.label: Screening
schema.text: Two steps: site confirms cancer type and treatment from the medical record, then the patient completes a confidential online self-reported screening survey and must receive an eligible result before OPEN enrollment.

schema.label: Main study assessments
schema.text: Online REDCap surveys: baseline, monthly for months 1-11, and expanded surveys at months 6 and 12 (13 total). Medical record abstraction at baseline and at least quarterly.

schema.label: Optional biospecimen sub-study (8 select sites)
schema.text: 100 ICI-treated participants (33 THC users, 33 CBD-only users, 34 never users). Past-week cannabis survey and blood draws before and 10 minutes before the end of the first ICI infusion, and 10 minutes before the end of the third ICI infusion.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Association between cannabis and/or cannabinoid use and cancer-related symptoms assessed monthly for one year.

eligibility: Age ≥18 with newly diagnosed breast cancer, colorectal cancer, melanoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or NSCLC (adenocarcinoma, squamous, large cell, adenosquamous, or NOS).
Planned systemic chemotherapy (single or multi-agent, including targeted therapy) and/or PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4 inhibitor; enrollment allowed up to the start of cycle 2.
Able to read English or Spanish, has a working email address, and is willing to complete surveys online.
Eligible result on the confidential self-reported screening survey; resides in the United States.
Life expectancy >6 months in the treating provider's opinion; not in hospice.
No current enrollment in an interventional supportive-care trial for cancer symptoms.
No prior systemic therapy (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted, or hormonal) for a prior cancer.
No known pregnancy.

Sub-study only: treated at a participating sub-study site, planning ICI therapy, baseline survey completed before the first ICI cycle; no chronic steroid or immunomodulatory therapy (chemotherapy premedication allowed) and no history of HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C.

during.window: Every 30 days from baseline survey, months 1-11

during.item: Medical record data forms (PFS, OS, treatment discontinuation for toxicity, select labs)
during.window: Months 3, 6, 9, and 12, or more often as needed

during.item: Sub-study blood draws and past-week cannabis survey

registry_schema.text: PLDR radiation technique has been shown to kill cancer cells while limiting normal tissue toxicity. In PLDR, subjects receive the same total dose of radiation for each treatment, but the treatment is delivered in a series of low-dose pulses which are separated by timed pauses. registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: One of the usual approaches to treating intermediate-risk prostate cancer is a type of radiation therapy called SBRT (stereotactic body radiation therapy). SBRT delivers higher than standard doses of radiation over a lower number of treatment sessions. However, there is a 20% chance that intermediate-risk prostate cancer will come back after this treatment. The purpose of this study is to find out whether giving an even higher dose (a "boost" dose) of radiation directly to the main tumor and the standard dose of radiation to the rest of the prostate may cure the cancer or prevent it from coming back for a longer period of time while causing few side effects.
